title: Great Barrier Reef Corals (Chromo V)
artist: William Saville-Kent (drawn and painted from life); chromolithograph printed by Riddle & Couchman, London
source: W. Saville-Kent, The Great Barrier Reef of Australia: its products and potentialities (London: W. H. Allen & Co., 1893). Smithsonian Libraries copy, digitised by the Internet Archive / Biodiversity Heritage Library.
license: Public domain (published 1893; the artist died in 1908)
note: Leaf 0090 JP2, 5751x7581. Cropped to the sheet inside the binding (the gutter, ribbon and page curl removed; a sliver of the toned fore-edge trimmed), about 4734x6991, resampled to 1800x2658 (Lanczos), WebP q90. This file is the finished state, and the last frame of the piece equals it.

title: The thirteen stones (coverage maps)
license: Public domain (derivative of a public-domain work)
note: The scan unmixed in optical density against its own paper into twelve inks (sparse dictionary learning, at most two inks per pixel), plus a key stone split from the dark inks' line work and the margin lettering. One 8-bit greyscale WebP per stone (q62); each stone's ink colour and scale are in reef.json.

title: The scraper's line and the ink's drying (time map)
note: Lossless WebP, half size. R: when the scraper's line reaches each point (down the sheet, slightly bowed, with the damp sheet's cockle). G: how long the fresh ink stays wet there (heavier deposits longer).
